notes:
Summary: AxialRift runs real-time personalization + bidding features for publisher ad slots. Extremely cost-sensitive at scale (100M+ requests/day) and latency-sensitive for UI flows and auctions. Exploring Redwood to reduce unit cost and get predictable tail latency across regions.

Key quote (CTO, Chris Novik): "We need p95 < 50ms for most requests and p99 < 120ms — any solution that spikes beyond that kills win-rate. Cost per 1M tokens needs to be under our current self-hosted baseline or we're not switching."

Requirements / constraints (from discovery + security):
- Workload: mix of short chat-like personalization prompts (avg tokens 12), reranking calls (prompt + 4-8 candidates), embeddings for semantic clustering (batch nightly), and real-time scoring for auctions (sub-100ms).
- Targets: p50 ~10-20ms, p95 <50ms, p99 <120ms at steady-state; sustained throughput target 2.5k QPS with bursts to 12k QPS.
- Cost sensitivity: looking for batching/caching/quantization guidance that reduces per-token cost 2x without regressing scoring quality >1% recall impact.
- Models: prefer open families (Mistral, LLaMA 2 variants); interested in Redwood-verified quantized variants (4-bit/8-bit) and fallback routing to cheaper models during regional capacity pressure.
- Deployment: VPC first; on-prem in EU/UK for regulated publisher partners (data residency). KMS integration mandatory. SOC2 + signed DPA required.

POC scope proposed (4 weeks):
1) Week 0: SE kickoff, ingest 72h production trace (anonymized) and baseline metrics.
2) Week 1: Redwood run: hosted API benchmark across 3 model variants (base open model, 8-bit quantized, 4-bit quantized) using dynamic batching + simulated KV/prefix-cache. Measure p50/p95/p99, throughput QPS, and cost per 1M tokens.
3) Week 2: Dedicated node proposal — test autoscaling policy, burst capacity, and fallbacks. Measure tail behavior under burst and sustained load.
4) Week 3: Integrate KMS + SSO test and produce security artifacts; present final recommendations including quantization profile, batching settings, and routing policy.

Specific optimization asks from AxialRift (what they want Redwood to demonstrate):
- Dynamic batching thresholds that keep p95 < 50ms while increasing throughput.
- KV/prefix cache hit-rate improvements for repeated personalization prefixes — show latency delta with/without cache.
- Quantization trade-offs: provide quality/regression metrics (A/B on reranking recall) and cost deltas for 8-bit and 4-bit options.
- Benchmark artifacts: scripts, raw CSV of latencies, token-level cost calc, and reproducible runbook.
